text: A.K. Fazlul Huq presented the Lahore resolution/Pakistan resolution in 1940

3. Perhaps the most surprising fact is that no manuscript of the speech exists. X was known for speaking extemporaneously without notes. The version we recognize today wasn't published until 1817—42 years after it was delivered.
Author William Wirt reconstructed the speech for a biography of X by interviewing elderly men who had been in the audience. Some historians argue Wirt may have "polished" or even invented parts of the prose to make it sound more heroic.
X didn't just say the words; he acted them out. According to witnesses, during the final line, X held an ivory letter opener (simulating a dagger) to his chest as if he were about to plunge it into his heart. The performance was so intense that after he finished, the room remained silent for several minutes. Id X and the speech.
Give me liberty, give me death ‎
